questions.question: What is the expected major product when 1,3-Butadiene is treated with HBr at low temperature (-80°C)?
questions.explanation: Treating 1,3-Butadiene with HBr at low temperature (-80°C) yields 3-Bromo-1-butene (1,2-kinetic product). Rationale: At low temperature, direct 1,2-addition via proximity of bromide to the allylic cation occurs with lowest activation energy.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of 1,3-Butadiene into 1-Bromo-2-butene (1,4-thermodynamic product)?
questions.explanation: To convert 1,3-Butadiene into 1-Bromo-2-butene (1,4-thermodynamic product), the appropriate reagent is HBr at elevated temperature (40°C). Rationale: At higher temperature, reversible addition yields the more substituted, thermodynamically more stable disubstituted alkene.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when 1,3-Butadiene + Maleic anhydride is treated with Heat (toluene, 80°C)?

options.label: B
options.text: 1,3-Butadiene absorbs at λmax = 217 nm (vs 171 nm for ethylene)

questions.explanation: Treating 1,3-Butadiene + Maleic anhydride with Heat (toluene, 80°C) yields cis-1,2,3,6-Tetrahydrophthalic anhydride. Rationale: Concerted [4+2] cycloaddition of s-cis diene with electron-deficient dienophile forms a cyclohexene ring.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Cyclopentadiene + Methyl acrylate into Methyl endo-bicyclo[2.2.1]hept-5-ene-2-carboxylate (major)?
questions.explanation: To convert Cyclopentadiene + Methyl acrylate into Methyl endo-bicyclo[2.2.1]hept-5-ene-2-carboxylate (major), the appropriate reagent is Room temperature. Rationale: Secondary orbital interactions between the carbonyl pi system and the developing diene pi system stabilize the endo transition state.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when (2Z,4Z)-2,4-Hexadiene + Maleic anhydride is treated with Heat?

options.label: C
options.text: 1,3-Butadiene absorbs at λmax = 217 nm (vs 171 nm for ethylene)

questions.explanation: Treating (2Z,4Z)-2,4-Hexadiene + Maleic anhydride with Heat yields No reaction (extremely slow). Rationale: Severe steric hindrance between terminal methyl groups prevents the diene from adopting the required s-cis conformation.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of 1,3-Cyclopentadiene into trans-1,4-Dibromo-2-cyclopentene (major)?
questions.explanation: To convert 1,3-Cyclopentadiene into trans-1,4-Dibromo-2-cyclopentene (major), the appropriate reagent is 1 equivalent Br2 in CCl4. Rationale: Electrophilic addition across the conjugated diene yields the allylic 1,4-dibromide.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with UV-Vis spectrophotometer to yield 1,3-Butadiene absorbs at λmax = 217 nm (vs 171 nm for ethylene) as the major product?
